title: Serre vanishing on projective space over a Noetherian ring
statement:
Let $A$ be Noetherian and $\mathcal F$ a
coherent module on
$P=\hyperref[def-pc-projective-space-twist]{\mathbf P^n_A}$.
There is $d_0\ge0$ such that $H^q(P,\mathcal F(d))=0$ for
all $d\ge d_0$ and all $q>0$.

proof.text: Proceed by descending induction on the cohomological degree q, simultaneously for all coherent modules. If q>n, the cohomology-bound node gives H^q(P, G)=0 for every quasi-coherent G, hence also after twisting. For q<=n, choose a short exact sequence 0 \to K \to direct sum_j O_P(-m_j) \to F \to 0 from the finite quotient-by-twists node. Since O_P(d) is invertible, tensoring this sequence with O_P(d) remains exact: locally the invertible module is free of rank one, so the tensor sequence is a copy of the original exact sequence. By the twist-tensor node, O_P(-m_j)\otimes O_P(d)\cong O_P(d-m_j), so the twisted middle term is direct sum_j O_P(d-m_j). The long exact cohomology sequence supplied by the cohomology-definition node then has consecutive terms direct sum_j H^q(P, O_P(d-m_j)) \to H^q(P, F(d)) \to H^{q+1}(P, K(d)).

For q>0, the left term vanishes once d >= max_j m_j by the positive-degree twisting-cohomology clause, because each d-m_j is nonnegative. The right term vanishes for all sufficiently large d by the descending induction hypothesis applied to the coherent kernel K. Thus a bound for degree q is the maximum of 0, the finitely many m_j, and the induction bound for K in degree q+1. Taking the maximum over q=1,...,n gives one bound d_0; when n=0 the cohomology-bound node already gives the result.
